messages:
anya: proposing a small, pragmatic design for vendor/tenant prioritizers. main trade: in-process for minimal p99 vs sidecar for safety and rapid iteration. want to capture handshake, fallback, telemetry, and rollout.

matt: agree we need a clear handshake and capability negotiation. sidecar is great for iteration but can add jitter. recommend default timeout 2ms and strict fallback.

kevin: if we allow in-process, require a tiny C shim to avoid language ABI pain. suggested signature: `int prioritize(const char* req_json, char** resp_json, int timeout_ms)`; runtime owns freeing resp_json. keeps runtime simple.

rachel: sidecar comms: prefer unix socket with framed JSON over HTTP/2 for multiplexing without heavy deps. require a version field and capabilities list in handshake (eg: supports_confidence, stream_ranking).

anya: minimal decision envelope we expect (for logs and tests): request_id, tenant_id, candidate list, hints blob. response: chosen, ranked list, per-candidate score, a concise reason string, and diagnostic_tags. keep payload compact but machine-readable.

matt: add per-candidate confidence and monotonic score so tie-breaks are deterministic. also include a short reason code for automatic tooling.

kevin: ops constraints: sidecar queue length must be monitored. if queue > 200, runtime should either fallback to builtin prioritizer or reject based on route criticality. add per-tenant admission controls. also set CPU/memory cgroup defaults for sidecars.

rachel: testing: add a sim harness that runs the builtin and sidecar decisions seeded identically; compute disagreement_rate and surface alerts. include e2e tests that inject slow sidecars to validate fallback behavior.

anya: rollout plan: 1) implement builtin prioritizer (weighted scoring + TTL cache). 2) sidecar runner image + shadow-only mode. 3) canary sidecar at 0.5-5% traffic with timeout and fallback. 4) allow tenant-managed sidecars after security review.

matt: security checklist: no network egress unless explicitly approved, verified SBOM, static analysis, thread/CPU caps. require policy-lint that flags disallowed ops before enabling a tenant plugin.

kevin: telemetry: minimal per-request labels (decision_id, tenant, chosen_route). sample full score_breakdown at 0.1% rate. metrics: prioritizer.latency_ms p50/p95/p99, prioritizer.fallback_rate, prioritizer.disagreement_rate. also emit spans for prioritize.call and sidecar_ms.

rachel: console UX: operator toggles per-tenant per-route for shadow vs active; disagreement dashboard and per-tenant limits visible. need an easy rollback toggle in case of regressions.

policy-bot: SECURITY REMINDER: customer plugins must pass Redwood plugin guidelines and security review. see internal link.

anya: open questions: typed hints vs freeform map; i propose structured core hints plus an extra_hints blob for experimental fields. also version the handshake so features can be gated.

matt: +1. we should default to structured core hints and allow safe extension via extra_hints.

kevin: will run perf tests on the shim prototype. ops will propose sane defaults for queue sizes and resource caps.

rachel: QA will own sim harness and disagreement alerts. will add regression thresholds for rollouts.

anya: next steps: draft proto/json schema, C shim spec, sidecar repo skeleton, and a canary runbook. will follow up with a short RFC PR. thanks all.
